blocks.text: The module documentation defines normalization, port, allowlist, prompting, persistence, cooldown, and logging rules. Constants establish bounded host/file/session limits and prompt answer vocabulary.
blocks.title: Network policy contract

blocks.text: Hosts are lowercased, IDNA-normalized, stripped of a trailing dot, and canonicalized for IP literals. parse_entry accepts exact names, explicit safe wildcards, or exact IPs while rejecting ambiguous forms.
blocks.title: Host and allowlist entry parsing

blocks.text: Allowlist stores exact names, wildcard bases, and IPs and matches normalized hosts. AllowFile validates ownership, mode, size, JSON shape, and entries, then writes permanent additions through an atomic 0600 replacement.
blocks.title: In-memory and saved allowlists

blocks.text: Decision carries an action and scope. command_label creates a short redacted prompt label and falls back to generic text whenever conversion or redaction fails.
blocks.title: Decisions and safe command labels

blocks.text: NetworkPolicy loads configured and saved approvals, validates ports and destinations, and returns allow, deny, or ask without prompting in check. decide adds prompting and decision recording.
blocks.title: Pure destination decisions

blocks.text: Prompt requests for the same host share one future, with a cap on distinct pending hosts. Answers update session or saved approvals; denials are remembered temporarily, and aclose cancels outstanding questions.
blocks.title: Prompt sharing and cooldowns

blocks.text: prompt_on_loop schedules the terminal prompt coroutine on another event loop and wraps it for the policy loop. Cancellation propagates back, and unknown answers become deny.
blocks.title: Cross-loop prompt bridge

gotchas: The saved file is user-level only and unsafe files are ignored.
A missing prompt turns ask into deny.
how_it_works: Canonicalizes host names and IP literals
Parses exact, wildcard, and IP allowlist entries
Checks configured, saved, and session approvals
Prompts with timeout and concurrency limits when needed
purpose: NetworkPolicy separates pure destination checks from prompting and persistence. It denies unsafe ports, local names, malformed or unlisted IP literals, shares concurrent prompts per host, cools down denials, and atomically saves permanent approvals.
summary: Normalizes network destinations, applies allowlists, and mediates interactive domain approval.
